notes: Fictional example -- exercises the qPCR/standard-curve field group using v3's standard-agnostic native names: standard_curve_slope, standard_curve_intercept, standard_curve_r_squared, qpcr_amplification_efficiency, assay_limit_of_detection. The text gives a dilution *range* for the standard rather than one input quantity, so qpcr_standard_concentration/qpcr_standard_concentration_unit are deliberately not expected here -- a range isn't a single value, and this case is meant to check the model doesn't fabricate one.
source_text: Absolute quantification was performed by qPCR using a standard curve generated from a tenfold dilution series of a synthetic gBlock gene fragment ranging from 10 to 10^6 copies/uL. The standard curve had a slope of -3.32, an intercept of 38.9, and an R-squared value of 0.998, corresponding to an amplification efficiency of 100%. The assay's limit of detection was 5 copies per reaction.

expected_facts.evidence_quote: limit of detection was 5 copies per reaction
